title: La nueva realidad de la educación ante los avances de la inteligencia artificial generativa / The new reality of education in the face of advances in generative artificial intelligence
venue: RIED-Revista Iberoamericana de Educación a Distancia
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the rapid emergence of generative AI, especially ChatGPT, and asks how these tools are reshaping education. Rather than evaluating a single intervention, the authors provide a reflective systematic review of the first six months of scientific output after ChatGPT’s release, alongside a map of contemporary generative-AI tools with possible educational uses. The paper’s main purpose is to balance enthusiasm and caution by identifying both the opportunities and the risks that generative AI introduces into teaching, learning, and educational governance.

The review surveys literature indexed in Web of Science and Scopus and organizes the findings around benefits, risks, and challenges for education. It discusses uses such as content generation, personalized support, tutoring-like dialogue, feedback, language learning, productivity support for teachers, and assessment innovation. At the same time, it highlights major concerns including hallucinations, plagiarism, privacy issues, bias, weak reliability of AI-text detectors, and possible erosion of critical thinking and interpersonal skills. The paper also catalogs specific tools across text, image, video, audio, code, and AI-detection categories, showing how quickly the ecosystem is expanding.

The educational contexts represented in the reviewed studies span several disciplines, including pre-university education, mathematics, and other fields, but the article itself is not a primary study of a specific student population. Its conclusions are strategic rather than experimental: institutions should not simply ban generative AI, but instead build policies, train teachers and students, revise curricula and assessment practices, and develop ethical guidance for responsible use. The authors argue that education must adapt quickly while preserving critical thinking, honesty, and human-centered pedagogy.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a reflective rapid review and conceptual paper, not a primary empirical study testing an intervention. It synthesizes early literature and policy discussion but provides no causal design, no participant-level data, and no quantitative effect estimates for the paper itself.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has clear relevance to current educational practice and policy around ChatGPT, but its contribution is mainly interpretive and strategic rather than evidence of measured learner gains. Any impact is therefore important for guidance and governance, but empirically uncertain.

interventions.use_case: Systematic review and conceptual analysis of ChatGPT and closely related generative AI chatbots as conversational learning assistants in education, including their use as virtual tutors, Q&A tools, and dialogue-based support for teaching and learning.

finding.finding_summary: This paper is a rapid review and reflective analysis of 31 education-related studies plus policy documents, not an effects study, so it does not report causal effect sizes. It concludes that generative AI in education creates both opportunities (personalization, productivity, new assessment models) and risks (academic integrity, bias, privacy, inequity), and argues institutions need guidance, training, and governance rather than prohibition.
finding.measure: Scope of reviewed literature; thematic synthesis of opportunities, risks, and policy/strategy implications
finding.study_size: n=31 studies in the review corpus (plus policy/position papers cited); not an intervention trial

finding.finding_summary: The review argues that generative AI tools can improve teacher productivity by reducing time spent answering repeated student questions, drafting materials, and grading written work, allowing staff to focus on higher-value feedback and support. No quantitative effect size is reported because this is a narrative synthesis rather than an experimental productivity study.
finding.measure: Reported teacher workload/productivity implications from reviewed studies
finding.study_size: n=31 studies in the review corpus; not_reported for productivity-specific estimates

finding.finding_summary: Across the reviewed literature, the authors note potential gains in critical thinking and creativity when students use generative AI to get feedback, explore ideas, and focus on higher-level reasoning. They also emphasize the opposite risk: overreliance may weaken independent thinking and creativity, so the net effect is presented as contingent and not yet empirically established.
finding.measure: Thematic claims about critical thinking, creativity, and independent reasoning
finding.study_size: n=31 studies in the review corpus; not_reported for skill outcomes
